title: Texas, yes Texas, puts limits on data centers
body: Texas is putting a halt to data center projects that try to tap into public utilities under new regulations issued by Governor Greg Abbott. The new order mandates the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) complete extensive audits of data center developers before they can connect to the state's utility grid. Notably, developers must provide information on "state and local tax incentives, grants, abatements, or other public financial assistance," prospective water and electricity use, and controlling interests in their projects. SEE ALSO: How 3 very different people use AI chatbots There are currently 1,800 projects awaiting ERCOT approval to join the state grid. Around 90 percent of them are for data centers, and the projects would cumulatively demand 474 gigawatts of electricity, according to the governor's office. The projected demand is more than five times the grid s peak record, reported the Texas Tribune . "Our top priority is to protect Texans safety and quality of life. Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT, and by state law, must be denied connection to the Texas grid. Simply put, Texans must come first," Abbott wrote in a press release issued Aug. 3. Texas has been beset by power outages in recent years, including an infamous power crisis in 2021 . Texas is home to over 500 data center projects , according to the tracking website Data Center Map. title: Texas halts data center connections to power grid amid overwhelming demand
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Nowhere is the US data center boom bigger than in Texas. But less than a year after declaring Texas the “epicenter of AI development,” Governor Greg Abbott has declared a moratorium on all new power grid connections for data centers—at least until developers provide more information about their projects’ potential impacts on the grid and communities. The Republican governor directed regulators in an August 3 announcement at the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the grid operators at the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to perform a “comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s interconnection process.” As an independent system operator, ERCOT oversees a power grid that operates separately from the rest of the United States and provides services to most of Texas. Texas has aggressively courted data center development with its availability of cheap land and relatively abundant energy resources, along with offering state incentives, like tax breaks and fewer regulations. That puts the state on track to surpass Virginia in becoming the largest US data center market . Read full article Comments

title: China is Tesla's cash cow, but for how much longer?
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Tesla's factory in Shanghai had its best June ever, according to the China Passenger ⁠Car Association. Tesla built 93,579 cars in China that month, a hefty 38 percent increase compared to June 2025, according to CPCA's data. But that production isn't translating into bumper sales to Chinese customers. Rather, sales have been down quarter on quarter in China for more than a year now, particularly as buyers tire of the Model 3 sedan . Almost 40 percent of the EVs that Tesla built in June were destined for export. And in Q2 in total, more than 50 percent—just—of the cars it built were for Europe, Canada, and other Asian markets: 128,394 versus the 126,157 Chinese-built Teslas that were sold to Chinese buyers. Low labor costs compared to Germany or the US are a big boon here, as are cheaper components from local suppliers. Throw in some export-related tax rebates from the Chinese government, and it's not hard to see how Tesla's Shanghai plant is an extremely valuable asset. Despite this seemingly critical importance to the automaker at a time when its profit margins are evaporating , Tesla may be contemplating a future without China. title: Microsoft warns hackers have compromised many hotel WiFi networks
body: Microsoft says the WiFi at your hotel might be compromised. In a post on its Threat Intelligence website (via ABC News ), Microsoft warned of a new hacking operation called "CaptiveCrunch," which the company claimed had some ties to Russia. Starting in May, Microsoft said it had observed a "widespread compromise of Wi-Fi networks at hospitality-related organizations," including WiFi networks at hotels. SEE ALSO: Microsoft Teams users will lose Calendar access in weeks unless they update The hacking operation works by tricking users to download malicious files via pop-ups that appear when connecting to a hotel WiFi network. Those who are doing this are able to get screenshots and keystrokes, and can even remotely hijack devices if necessary. There are also fake login screens that could give the hackers access to a user's personal email address. According to Microsoft, the best way to avoid this is to use something more private when traveling, like a mobile hotspot. If that's not an option and you must use hotel WiFi, be on the lookout for any kind of pop-up window that appears after logging into the network. These can appear as Windows Update pop-ups or other kinds of update windows you might normally see on your device, but if they appear right as you've logged into hotel WiFi, they might be up to something. In other words, if you aren't expecting any kind of update pop-up, maybe avoid any of them that appear.

title: Using the Apple Upgrade program locks you into the big three mobile providers
body: Apple's new device-leasing program has a strange (on the surface) rule attached to it. Last week, Apple launched Apple Upgrade , a new Klarna-backed program that allows customers to lease new iPhones, MacBooks, and other devices for a small-ish monthly payment, rather than spending more than $1,000 up front. However, folks quickly noticed something in the fine print: You'll need an account with AT T, Verizon, or T-Mobile to lease an iPhone. Our big Guessing Game is back! Enter for a chance to win an Apple Watch . So, while the phones are technically unlocked, you can only activate them with one of the big three mobile carriers. Cybersecurity analyst John Gruber looked into this and, on his website, Daring Fireball , gave a couple of big reasons as to why that might be the case. title: Trump admin "aware" of deaths in explosive diarrhea outbreak, delays reporting
author: Beth Mole
body: Two people have died amid the ongoing record-breaking outbreak of explosive diarrhea from the foodborne parasite Cyclospora , Michigan health officials announced Monday. Cyclosporiasis fatalities are extremely rare, and despite the massive size of the outbreak, some experts were still surprised by the deaths. The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services on Monday said that medical records of both individuals indicated that they had "significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration." MDHHS noted that both fell ill with the diarrheal infection before Taylor Farms recalled its shredded iceberg lettuce grown in Mexico, which has been linked to thousands of cases in at least nine states. Cyclospora is a unicellular parasite that spreads in human feces and is often transmitted via contaminated fresh produce, such as lettuces and other fruits and vegetables that have uneven surfaces for the parasite to grip. Past culprits have included fresh herbs, raspberries, green onions, and snow peas. Read full article Comments

body: The Hatch Restore 3 smart alarm clock helped Mashable Senior Shopping Reporter Leah Stodart regulate her bedtime routine. And as of Aug. 4, the brand has dropped a new device to improve sleep. The Hatch Sleep Clock isn't just another smart alarm clock; it's a contactless sleep tracker . At launch, the Hatch Sleep Clock is exclusively available at hatch.co for $249.99, and will be available from other retailers, including Amazon, later this year. Getting to know the Hatch Sleep Clock Unlike a Whoop or Oura tracker, the Hatch Sleep Clock is obviously not a wearable . It sits on your nightstand and uses ultra-low-power radio signals to detect breathing and movement (no microphone required). It can track when you go to bed, fall asleep, and wake up throughout the night. According to a study , the tech behind the Sleep Clock is 97 percent accurate at sleep detection. The Hatch Sleep Clock tracks sleep from your bedside table. Credit: Hatch The Hatch Sleep Clock combines sleep insights with the other tech Hatch is known for: immersive light, sleep audio, and personalized routines. "We didn't set out to build another sleep tracker. We set out to help people sleep better," said Ann Crady Weiss, Co-Founder and CEO of Hatch, in a press release. "Rather than simply reporting what happened last night, Hatch Sleep Clock gets you to bed tonight." title: How much is Spotify Premium in the U.S.?
body: Everything is better without ads ruining the vibe, and your perfect playlist deserves to play on uninterrupted. Don't believe us? As of August 2026, Spotify had 300 million Premium subscribers enjoying ad-free songs, podcasts, and audiobooks. Here's how each of the platform's Premium plans break down. What do I get with a free Spotify account? You'll have access to Spotify's music library, but you'll have to listen to ads and won't be able to download music to your phone for times when you don't have W-Fi access (like on planes). What do I get with a Spotify Premium plan? If you want an ad-free and offline listening experience, Premium is the way to go. You'll get ad-free access to Spotify's entire music library, 15 hours of audiobook listening time, and the ability to download music and podcasts to your device. Plus, you'll get access to lossless audio , be able to play songs in any order, and listening queue options, none of which are available on Spotify's free plan. In recent years, Spotify has added a huge amount of extra features to tempt free users to pay for Premium, including Page Match (to move between physical books and audiobooks), Running Mode , concert tickets sales , as well as an AI chatbot to unpack your music and listening history . "I'm sure this stance will be applied equally to all other apps in the store, in the future right?" read the post, tagging Apple's official account. Telegram continued in the same tone on its main page, posting "reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated" along with an apple emoji. This Tweet is currently unavailable. body: Snap held its Q2 2026 earnings call on Monday, with CEO Evan Spiegel speaking about the company's hopes and the public's response to its upcoming Specs AR glasses . Currently available for pre-order, Snap's Specs are scheduled to launch on Sept. 16 and will set buyers back the formidable sum of $2,195. It's an intimidating price tag which may scare off some consumers. Still, Spiegel believes Specs are the future of Snap. The company has invested significantly in the AR glasses, which have been in development for over 10 years, and sees Specs as an important milestone. SEE ALSO: All about the Specs AR glasses, with Snap CEO Evan Spiegel "Our largest long-term opportunity is Specs, a new kind of computer built into see-through glasses," Spiegel said early in Monday's earnings call. "Specs are designed for a future in which AI does more work on our behalf and people spend less time operating screens." Despite this vision, it's unclear whether public anticipation for Specs' release is meeting Snap's expectations. When asked about pre-order volumes, Spiegel claimed there has been "a huge amount of interest" in the AR glasses since they were announced in June . Even so, he did not offer any exact numbers, leaving it ambiguous as to whether such interest has materially translated into pre-orders. "What we're hearing from folks is really that they want to try Specs," said Spiegel. "It's obviously a high consideration purchase at $2,195." body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: Review: ‘Beast of Reincarnation’ is fun but it won’t outgrow ‘Pokémon’ anytime soon
body: Game Freak s enduring legacy is being the developer of the Pok mon franchise alongside Nintendo. While that certainly has its perks like keeping the office lights on, it shouldn t be surprising that Game Freak wants to branch out. It s been done so over the years with smaller games like Giga Wrecker Alt , Little Town Hero , and Tembo the Badass Elephant . Now, Game Freak is back with the action-adventure game Beast of Reincarnation . It s the studio s biggest game yet, but is it big enough to step out from Pok mon s massive shadow? The combat is sublime, along with its breathtaking art direction and intriguing open-world zones. However, Beast of Reincarnation is muzzled by its confusing story pacing and dull cast of characters. Not Nier enough Credit: Game Freak / Screenshot by George Yang Beast of Reincarnation follows a young girl named Emma as she travels through a post-apocalyptic Japan to stop the titular monster from rising again and spreading a corruption called Blight. Much like Stellar Blade , Beast of Reincarnation attempts to emulate the profound themes of existentialism, artificial intelligence, sentience, and humanity found in the excellent Nier: Automata . But they fail to understand what made Yoko Taro s masterpiece so compelling: the characters. Emma isn t exactly a riveting character up until the last few moments of the story. At that point, there s a giant exposition dump explaining about how the world came to be. title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Ukrainian drone operators have destroyed many Russian armored vehicles on the ground and even military helicopters in midair using $400 Shrike drones with explosive payloads. Now thousands of such drones are getting upgraded with an AI system capable of autonomously tracking and homing in on moving targets. In mid-July, the Ukrainian military began receiving Shrike drones made by the Ukrainian company SkyFall equipped with AI-powered autonomy hardware and software developed by the US company Auterion. The companies plan to deliver 50,000 drones equipped with Auterion’s Skynode S strike kits in the coming months. That allows human operators to manually fly the Shrike first-person view (FPV) drones into a battlefield area, designate a target up to half a mile away and then “flip the switch to turn it into fire-and-forget terminal guidance mode,” Lorenz Meier , co-founder and CEO of Auterion, told Ars. title: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks. July’s list includes outfitting cyborg cockroaches with a tiny diving suit for navigating flooded terrain; confirmation that a Medici duke died of malaria, not poisoning; the best evidence to date that Betelgeuse is orbited by a companion star; and evidence that some ancient Egyptian princesses were skilled archers. Sacrificial Incan boy died of blunt force trauma Credit: Administrative Archive, Regional Museum of Iquique–CORMUDESI It's known that the Incas practiced a human sacrifice ritual known as Capachoca, in which children were offered to the mountains and believed to become divine themselves, serving as intermediaries with the gods. This often involved pilgrimages to the remote sacrificial sites, with colonial accounts describing strangulation, asphyxiation, and blunt force trauma as the most common methods of sacrifice. Archaeologists have reanalyzed the remains of one such victim and concluded the boy died from blunt force trauma, rather than freezing to death as previously believed. They described their findings in a paper published in the journal Science Advances. Read full article Comments

A bad one can set the tone for an entire relationship, whether that's with a person, a novel, a restaurant, or a car. And the 2026 Volkswagen Jetta Sport and I did not get off to the best of starts. body: Who says the meet cute is dead ? According to Eventbrite, it's facing a revival. Hobby-based events using language like "singles," "come solo," and "find your people" are also on the rise. And the hobbies that Eventbrite is seeing take off are pretty wholesome. Mahjong events are up 235 percent, and attendance is up 272 percent. Trivia night events have skyrocketed 403 percent, with a 388 percent increase in attendance. Bird watching, Pilates socials, plant swaps and workshops, and pottery and craft circles are among the events people are flocking to. In its blog post about the findings, Eventbrite theorizes that singles are craving spontaneous connections in our algorithmically driven world, and that niche hobbies are what stand out today. title: Bluesky’s new CEO wants a big tent, not a bubble
body: Today, I’m talking with Toni Schneider, who is the brand new CEO of the social platform Bluesky — he formally took over after a short stint as interim CEO. This is one of my favorite kinds of interviews to do on Decoder , because a couple years ago, we had Bluesky’s prior CEO, Jay Graber, on the show — she’s now the company’s chief innovation officer, and all of that kind of shuffle is pure Decoder bait. And a new CEO often brings with them new priorities, which is perhaps the most Decoder subject of all. Bluesky in particular is a company pulling in a lot of different directions: There’s a Twitter-like social media app, which is what most people are familiar with, and then there’s the underlying technology behind that app call AT Protocol, which allows anyone to build social networking products that interoperate with Bluesky. As you’ll hear Toni say, that ecosystem is vibrant and growing — it’s called the ATmosphere, which is adorable. But the users of Bluesky the app are not the same as the people building on AT Protocol, and the goals of a company founded to push forward the ideas of open and interoperable social standards are not necessarily aligned with the things all those users might need or want. This is a fight that bursts into view on Bluesky itself all the time, and I wanted to know how Toni thinks about balancing all of that with what remains a fairly small team. It’ll work fine without a heatsink in a PC or laptop (though, it’s never a bad idea to use one that fits in your system). body: The MCU's Blade movie is dead. Mahershala Ali told GQ , "If they wanted to do it, we would've done it." But fret not. If you want Ali delivering hard-hitting action as an anti-hero, behold the trailer for Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. From writer-director Bassam Tariq, who was attached to helm the Blade movie back in 2021, comes this original film, part crime thriller and part family drama. Ali stars as a hitman who strives to protect his Muslim community with his sword. But when his wife dies, his priorities shift as he becomes a single father to three children, including an infant in need of mother's milk. He's grappling with grief, struggling with his faith, and seeking to feed his children. And that's when he crosses paths with a Christian militia leader, played by John Cho . Abubakr Ali, Laith Nakli, Tramell Tillman, Tiffany Boone, and Giancarlo Esposito, Adia, and Jahleel Kamara co-star. title: Trump wants the power to stop the public from suing polluters
author: Sarah J. Morath, The Conversation
body: Reducing rampant pollution across the United States was so important that when Congress passed many environmental protection laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and Safe Drinking Water Act, it didn’t want to leave enforcement only to the executive branch. Congress specifically wrote into those laws ways for citizens to enforce them through the courts when the government does not act to address the problem. Called “ citizen suit provisions ,” those parts of the laws allow regular people and advocacy groups to sue companies they believe are violating the law. Citizens can also sue federal agencies that fail to enforce the laws. Since the 1970s, those provisions have been used in over 2,000 lawsuits . In fact, a majority of environmental cases are citizen suit cases. Citizen suits have been used to halt the construction of dams to protect endangered species , end the injection of wastewater into groundwater , and secure US$14.2 million in civil penalties for illegal emissions from a petrochemical facility. In short, these cases have shaped modern environmental law. Read full article Comments

title: How headlights got brighter, whiter, and more blinding after dark
author: Matthew MacConnell
body: Every so often, I’ll be piloting some sensor-laden, software-defined press car down a dark stretch of highway when an oncoming driver’s high beams arrive like a targeted retinal strike, an involuntary reminder that modern automotive lighting has entered its own lumen arms race. Anyone who has driven at night in the last few years knows what I'm talking about: A modern crossover crests a hill in the opposite lane, and the cabin briefly fills with enough cold-white light to suggest a police helicopter has joined traffic. The obvious assumption is that drivers are simply leaving their high beams on more often, but the reality is more complicated. An old problem Before cars became the modern mode of transportation, horse-drawn carriages used oil lanterns to light the way, as roads were largely unlit outside of towns and cities. These lanterns weren’t particularly bright, though, meaning that after-dark collisions and near-misses were common. Read full article Comments

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 3
body: The Moon is now losing more of its light, with the next major milestone in its cycle being the Third Quarter phase. Here's what you can spot on its surface tonight. What is today s Moon phase? As of Monday, Aug. 3, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Gibbous phase, with 79% of its surface visible. With just your naked eye, tonight you can spot the Copernicus Crater and the Tycho Crater. If you have a pair of binoculars, these will help you see the Alphonsus Crater, Mare Humorum, and the Mare Frigoris. Finally, if you have a telecope, this will help you see the Apollo 11, 14 and 15 landing spots. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? According to NASA , the Moon goes through a complete cycle of eight phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it travels around Earth, the angle between the Sun, Earth and Moon constantly changes, meaning we see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit side. This is what causes the familiar progression from a thin crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the cycle repeats. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Alternate Wordle versions created by fans also sprang up, including battle royale Squabble , music identification game Heardle , and variations like Dordle and Quordle that make you guess multiple words at once . Wordle eventually became so popular that it was purchased by the New York Times , and TikTok creators even livestream themselves playing . What's the best Wordle starting word? title: Snapchat is the latest platform to turn against AI slop
body: Snapchat is officially joining the race to clean AI slop out of social media . The company announced July 31 that wholly AI-generated videos will no longer be eligible for recommendation in Spotlight, Snapchat s discovery feed for trending videos from creators across the platform in order to "reward authentic creativity." The policy does not prevent users from posting AI-generated videos elsewhere on Snapchat. It also does not disqualify every video that involves AI. Creators can continue using Snapchat s AI tools to edit or enhance their original footage, and those videos will remain eligible for Spotlight recommendations with transparency indicators. SEE ALSO: New safety rules for under-16 Snapchat users The line Snapchat is drawing comes down to who, or what, created the underlying video. AI can help a person make something. It cannot make the entire thing and still expect Snapchat s recommendation system to distribute it. "As low-quality, repetitive, AI-generated content becomes increasingly common across the internet, we want Spotlight to remain a place where people can discover authentic creativity from real people," the company wrote in a blog post. Keeping entirely generated videos out of Spotlight matters on the platform because recommendation is what allow a creator s work to reach people who do not already follow them. Removing that distribution makes Spotlight far less valuable as a growth channel for automated content farms that can produce synthetic videos at scale. title: Minnesotas nudification ban takes effect after judge rejects xAIs bid to pause it
body: Minnesota's new ban on AI "nudification" technology took effect on August 1, 2026, after a federal judge declined to pause it, even as a legal challenge by Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI, proceeds. U.S. District Judge Donovan W. Frank denied xAI's emergency motion for a temporary restraining order in a two-page order issued July 31 . The judge found that the company's own timeline undercut its claim of urgent harm, noting that xAI filed its motion "nearly three months after the law was signed, and only three days before the law is set to take effect." SEE ALSO: Teens sue xAI for Grok's reported sexual image generation issues The order stated that such a delay "suggests that harm is not immediate," and cited a prior Minnesota case in which a similar delay weighed against granting emergency relief. Minnesota's nudification law, explained The statute, H.F. 1606 , adds a new section to Minnesota law prohibiting any person who owns or controls a website, app, or software from allowing users to "nudify" images or generate such alterations on a user's behalf. It also bars advertising or promoting services that perform this function. The bill defines "nudify" as altering or generating an image so that it depicts an intimate part not present in the original, in a way realistic enough that a reasonable viewer would believe it belonged to the person shown. The law carves out an exemption for tools that require "the technical skill of a user" to produce the alteration, and it preserves Section 230 liability protections under federal law. body: What is the best Dyson vacuum cleaner? Regardless of your living situation, I believe the best Dyson vacuum cleaner is a cordless stick vacuum. Dyson hasn't made a new corded vacuum since 2018 , and it doesn't plan on updating the line in the future. If you were waffling between a corded vs. cordless design, at least that part of the decision has been made for you. For a while, Dyson Ball vacuums had such impressive suction that people simply put up with their bulkiness and the major inconvenience of being tethered to the wall. But in 2026, cordless Dyson vacuums are far too powerful and agile to make the old cumbersome design worth the hassle. In fact, the new Dyson V16 Piston Animal has officially surpassed the suction power of any corded Dyson vacuum. Past that, the best Dyson cordless vacuum for one household may not be the best cordless Dyson for another household. The best fit is highly dependent on factors like the size of your home, your floor type, the number of pets that you have, and the amount of money you feel like spending. Do you need a full suite of attachments and dust-detecting lasers to match your (clean) freak, or would you prefer a more affordable version that just does the job? I have a solid idea of both ends of the Dyson spectrum from personal experience, and from comparing the value of the Dyson lineup to other top cordless vacuum cleaners from brands like Shark. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 2
body: The Moon is still in its waning gibbous phase following the Full Moon. Here's what you can see on its surface tonight. What is today s Moon phase? As of Sunday, Aug. 2, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Gibbous phase, with 87% of its surface visible. You don't need to have lots of visual equipment to see features on the Moon's surface. In fact, with just your naked eye you can spot the Oceanus Procellarum, Kepler Crater, and Mare Vaporum tonight. However, visual aids do make the experience more advanced, so if you have a pair of binoculars, this will help you see the Alphonsus Crater, Mare Humorum, and the Mare Frigoris. Pull out your telescope (if you have one) to see see all clearer, plus the Apollo 15 landing spot, the Rima Ariadaeus, and the Schiller Crater. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? According to NASA , the Moon goes through a complete cycle of eight phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it travels around Earth, the angle between the Sun, Earth and Moon constantly changes, meaning we see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit side. This is what causes the familiar progression from a thin crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the cycle repeats. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). title: Here's how engineers plan to save the satellite sent to save NASA's Swift mission
author: Stephen Clark
body: One week ago, more than 200 miles above the Earth, a refrigerator-size satellite making its way toward an attempted rescue of NASA's $500 million Swift gamma-ray observatory suddenly spun out of control . It didn't look good. The spacecraft, named Link, was rotating on multiple axes, rendering it unable to maintain a reliable communications link with the ground and complicating efforts to arrest the spin. Two of the satellite's three reaction wheels, used for pointing, also stopped working. Through sporadic radio contact, engineers discovered a problem with some of the spacecraft's cold gas thrusters used for finer attitude control. The Link satellite is built, owned, and operated by Katalyst Space Technologies, a satellite servicing startup that won a $30 million contract from NASA to fly up to the Swift observatory, grab onto it, and boost its orbit before succumbing to aerodynamic drag and burning up int he atmosphere. title: Sam Altman suggests parents generate AI podcasts about their kids
body: OpenAI founder and CEO Sam Altman is trending on X for suggesting that parents use ChatGPT to generate podcasts about their children's lives in lieu of... listening to them. "cool use case of chatgpt work i heard last night," he shared on X in all lowercase . "connect your family calendars and explain your kids' interests." SEE ALSO: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was worse than we thought He continued, "Every morning for the drive to school, have it make a podcast that talks about one kid's soccer game that afternoon, one kid's upcoming birthday, some news, etc." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. The post has amassed around 9,500 likes at the time of this writing, dwarfed by 120,000 likes on the reply, "What if you just talked to your children?" from Gravity Falls creator Alex Hirsch . (The same day, Hirsch also criticized Google's addition of its AI image generator into Google Earth , which it reversed.) Other popular replies have the same sentiment: That Altman is apparently encouraging users to disconnect from their families. The backlash about AI tools has ramped up in recent years, for a myriad of reasons, including environmental impacts , surveillance , job loss , and fears of AI psychosis . The potential degrading of relationships is also a concern for some, as more people turn to chatbots to outsource relational conflicts or even seek to replace relationships themselves. title: Review: Yes, we're still arguing about Nolan's The Odyssey
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has been a lightning rod for controversy ever since the first casting and design reveals, igniting afresh with each new trailer . The film has garnered plenty of well-deserved accolades ( and earnings ) since its release, and yet somehow the debates rage on between classicists and the general public alike—all this over an adaptation of an epic poem that's been around since roughly the 8th century BCE. My take: the IMAX scale might be epic, but Nolan gives the story an intimate feel, weaving a captivating, nearly three-hour cinematic spell. While the magic slowly starts to dissipate once one leaves the theater, the powerful imagery will resonate for days. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for August 1, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible and common for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels: Number : All the pips in this space must add up to the number. title: Google rolls back AI Google Earth feature a day after launch
body: After Google added its AI image generator, Nano Banana, to Google Earth on Thursday, it reversed its decision a day later. Google announced the addition of Nano Banana 2 into its mapping platform, presumably to help users generate infographics about a site, see what it looked like historically, generate real estate ideas, and other use cases. Instead, as 404 Media observed, it made it very easy to inject misinformation into Google Earth , including making it appear like a nuclear strike had hit a location or that protests had taken over Google's offices. SEE ALSO: Reminder: Don't use Google Maps for hiking On Thursday, Google seemed to try to smooth out the kinks, sharing on Thursday night on X that "every image created with Nano Banana in Google Earth includes the SynthID digital watermark, so if someone is unsure about an image, they can ask the Gemini app or use Lens in Search to see if the image was AI-generated." It also stated that it prevents image creation on "harmful topics." However, come Friday afternoon, Google announced on X that it was removing the feature: We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world. We've seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes, however we've also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies. So we're rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails. title: New York sues Kalshi, claiming its unlicensed gambling
body: On Friday, New York state filed a lawsuit against prediction market platform Kalshi, claiming that it's operating as an "unlicensed gambling business." The Office of Attorney General Letitia James found that Kalshi is an illegal prediction market that exposes New Yorkers to "serious personal and financial risk," according to a press release. The lawsuit seeks fines, the forfeit of all illegal gains, and restitution to members. SEE ALSO: Kalshi gains 3 million users amid World Cup gambling The suit claims that Kalshi's prediction markets meet the legal definition of gambling "because the outcomes of the events on which its users are betting are uncertain and outside the control of the bettor or hinge on a game of chance." But the platform hasn't obtained a license from the New York State Gaming Commission. It also states that Kalshi is available to adults aged 18-20, while New York law requires users to be at least 21 to bet on sports. "Kalshi has chosen to ignore New York s gaming laws, which exist to protect consumers, prevent problematic gambling, deliver funding for critical public services, and ensure that every company plays by the same rules," New York Governor Kathy Hochul said in the press release. "This choice has consequences, and working closely with Attorney General James, New York is taking action to stop this illegal behavior and bring Kalshi into compliance, because no company is above the law."
